provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite provider; accounting SaaS provider
implementation_statement: The SaaS providers supply account functions. The owner holds the only productivity suite account and the administrator account in the accounting SaaS; the bookkeeper has a named accountant login. Gap: the laptop has one administrator account used for daily work, the IT technician's remote-support account was never reviewed, and no one reviews accounts on a schedule.

The productivity suite enforces sharing permissions and the accounting SaaS enforces the accountant role. Gap: file sharing defaults to "anyone with the link" with no expiry, so drawings shared with outside processors stay open indefinitely.
evidence: Sharing settings; list of open links (27 found 2026-08-11)

implementation_statement: The only remote access is the IT technician's remote-support tool on the laptop. Unattended access was on until the owner turned it off during the assessment on 2026-08-12. Gap: no written rule for remote sessions; the technician's tool account MFA is unconfirmed.

Customer portals are used under the customers' own terms. Gap: no list of approved external systems. Customer drawing content went to a consumer AI assistant (SYS-08), and aerospace drawings were emailed to the anodizer.
evidence: Email sent-items review; AI assistant chat history (P10)

implementation_statement: Only the owner can post to the website. A gallery photo of an aerospace part with its part number visible was found and removed on 2026-08-12. Gap: no review before posting and no periodic content check.
The owner has had no security training. The owner will complete a free small-business cybersecurity course and subscribe to a monthly security reminder by 2026-11-30.

implementation_statement: The providers record sign-ins and admin events. No one has ever looked at them. From 2026-10 the owner will review sign-in history for email and accounting on the first workday of each month.
The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gap: no emergency access sheet and no written overflow arrangement with another shop (due 2026-12-31).

implementation_statement: The productivity suite keeps deleted items and file versions for 30 days and the provider backs up its own service. regulatory_driver: OEM SQA (10-year record retention); CSF 2.0 benchmark (PR.DS-11)

implementation_statement: Default passwords are changed on SaaS accounts. Gap: the owner reuses two passwords across services and has no password manager; the router admin password was the factory default until 2026-08-12.
The ransomware runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-09-04 with customer notice terms. Gap: contacts not printed; never walked through (due 2026-10-15).
regulatory_driver: Aerospace PO terms (72-hour incident notice); OEM SQA (5-business-day notice)

implementation_statement: No procedure. The laptop replaced in 2025 still holds old job files, and used USB sticks are thrown away as they are.

Programs for the turning center move on USB sticks written on the laptop, whose antivirus scans them. Gap: sticks are unlabeled and mixed with personal sticks; the service technician's laptop connects to the VMC with no check.

The bay is locked with a monitored alarm; the owner holds the keys and the landlord a master key. Gap: visitors (auditors, service technician, drivers) are not escorted by rule and drawings lie on the bench in view.
No visitor log. A paper visitor log at the door, kept one year, starts 2026-09-15.
First risk assessment completed 2026-08-14 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed every August and after a major change.

NDAs with the four main customers and with the IT technician (2026-08-07). The productivity suite provider's SOC 2 report was read on 2026-08-13 (P09). Gap: outside processors have no confidentiality or FAR 52.204-21 terms; the AI assistant runs under consumer terms.

The router blocks unsolicited inbound traffic and the laptop firewall is on. Gap: one flat network for the laptop, VMC, alarm panel, and visitors; the VMC program share on the laptop accepts connections without a password; the router admin password was the default until 2026-08-12.
The laptop uses built-in full-disk encryption (confirmed 2026-08-12); the phone is encrypted by its passcode; the SaaS providers encrypt stored data (SOC 2 report, P09).
evidence: Encryption status screen; vendor SOC 2 report

provider_if_inherited: Laptop and phone OS vendors; SaaS providers
implementation_statement: Automatic OS updates on the laptop and phone; the SaaS providers patch their services. Gap: the CAM software is two releases behind, router firmware was never updated, and the VMC controller software is no longer supported (a specialized asset; compensated by network separation).
Built-in antivirus runs real-time and scheduled scans with automatic updates, including files on USB sticks and downloads. Owner responsibility: keep it on and act on alerts.

Released programs for OEM parts are not protected from change: edits at the controller leave no record and there is no compare against the released copy. Plan: a read-only Released folder with file hashes, and a compare before each run of an OEM job (by 2026-12-31).
regulatory_driver: OEM SQA (no change to released processes without approval)
